1: # Tiered Memory System — Short / Mid / Long-Term (Flagship Feature)
2: 
3: Three-layer memory architecture so the app behaves like it genuinely knows the user and the work — not just "remembers the last N messages." Runs entirely silently (per the orchestrator's silent-mode precedent) — no UI exposure of internal memory state during chat, except one optional settings panel for transparency/trust (§7). This is designed as the app's core differentiator, so the long-term layer gets the deepest treatment.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## Why Layered (not one flat memory blob)
8: 
9: A single sliding-window/summarization scheme (already planned in `context-length-handling.md`) has a critical flaw for this use case: **an important rule stated early in a long conversation can get silently dropped or diluted once it's compacted away with everything else.** If a user says "don't use semicolons in code you write me" on message 3 of a 200-message session, that instruction must survive to message 200 — it can't be treated the same as ordinary chat content that's fine to summarize away. Splitting memory into three purpose-built layers, each with different persistence rules and injection guarantees, solves this directly.
10: 
11: | Layer | Scope | Survives sliding-window truncation? | Survives session end? |
12: |---|---|---|---|
13: | **Short-term** | Current turn/task, active rules & constraints | Yes — never truncated, injected every turn | No — session-scoped |
14: | **Mid-term** | Goals, plans, project structure for this session | Yes — this *is* what compaction produces | No (by default) — but see §6 for promotion to long-term |
15: | **Long-term** | Who the user is, across all sessions | N/A (not part of the sliding window at all) | Yes — persists indefinitely, consolidated over time |
16: 
17: ---
18: 
19: ## Layer 1 — Short-Term Memory (Active Rules & Immediate Context)
20: 
21: ### What it holds
22: - Explicit rules/constraints the user has stated ("don't do X", "always respond in Thai", "for this project, never suggest Y")
23: - Immediate task focus (what the current exchange is actually about, right now)
24: - Urgent one-off instructions ("for the next answer only, be extremely brief")
25: 
26: ### Data model
27: ```rust
28: struct ActiveConstraint {
29:     id: Uuid,
30:     session_id: Uuid,
31:     text: String,                  // normalized instruction, e.g. "avoid semicolons in generated code"
32:     scope: ConstraintScope,        // Session | ThisTurnOnly
33:     created_at: DateTime,
34:     superseded_by: Option<Uuid>,   // if a later message contradicts/updates this one
35: }
36: 
37: enum ConstraintScope {
38:     Session,       // "from now on", "always", "for this project" — persists whole session
39:     ThisTurnOnly,  // "just this once", "for this answer" — auto-expires after one generation
40: }
41: ```
42: 
43: ### Extraction (runs after every user turn, cheap)
44: - Lightweight pattern/heuristic classifier first (imperative phrasing: "don't", "always", "never", "from now on", "for this project") — cheap, no model call needed for the common case
45: - Escalate to a small model-based classification only when the heuristic is ambiguous, similar cost-gating approach as the orchestrator's query decomposition
46: - On detecting a new constraint that **contradicts** an existing active one, mark the old one `superseded_by` the new — never silently keep two conflicting rules both active
47: 
48: ### Injection guarantee
49: - All `Session`-scoped active constraints for the current session are **always** included in the system prompt, in a **fixed, reserved token budget** separate from the conversation-history/evidence budget in `context_manager.rs` — this budget is small (constraints are short) but non-negotiable; it is never trimmed by the sliding window or context-pressure logic
50: - `ThisTurnOnly` constraints are injected once, then discarded immediately after that generation completes
51: 
52: ### Integration point
53: `src-tauri/src/engine/memory/short_term.rs` (new) — sits alongside `context_manager.rs`, exposes `active_constraints(session_id) -> Vec<ActiveConstraint>` that `context_manager.rs` calls when composing every prompt, before it does its normal history-budget allocation.
54: 
55: ---
56: 
57: ## Layer 2 — Mid-Term Memory (Goals, Plans, Project Structure)
58: 
59: ### What it holds
60: Structured (not prose-blob) tracking of what the current session is actually trying to accomplish:
61: ```rust
62: struct SessionMemory {
63:     session_id: Uuid,
64:     goals: Vec<Goal>,
65:     decisions: Vec<Decision>,
66:     open_questions: Vec<String>,
67:     plan_steps: Vec<PlanStep>,
68: }
69: 
70: struct Goal {
71:     description: String,
72:     status: GoalStatus,           // Active | Achieved | Abandoned
73: }
74: 
75: struct Decision {
76:     what: String,                 // "using SQLite for local storage"
77:     why: Option<String>,          // "no server process needed, good Rust support"
78:     turn_ref: usize,              // which message this came from, for traceability
79: }
80: 
81: struct PlanStep {
82:     description: String,
83:     status: StepStatus,           // Pending | InProgress | Done
84: }
85: ```
86: 
87: This upgrades the flat `conversation_memory: TEXT` field already in the `sessions` table (per `chat-session-management-plan.md`) into structured JSON — still one column, but the app can now reason over it (e.g. "3 plan steps done, 2 pending") instead of just re-reading prose.
88: 
89: ### Extraction
90: - Runs as a background/opportunistic compaction step — same trigger point already planned for conversation-memory summarization (idle time between messages, or right before the sliding window would need to drop old turns)
91: - The compaction call is prompted to extract structure, not just summarize prose: "what goals, decisions, and plan steps are evident from this conversation so far" — output parsed into the `SessionMemory` struct above
92: - Updates are **merges, not overwrites** — new extraction runs reconcile against the existing `SessionMemory` (mark completed goals as `Achieved`, append new decisions, don't duplicate ones already recorded)
93: 
94: ### Injection
95: - A compact rendering of `SessionMemory` (a few lines, not the full structured JSON) goes into the system prompt every turn, in its own modest reserved budget — smaller than short-term's constraint budget priority-wise, but still guaranteed a slice rather than competing directly with raw conversation history for space
96: - This is what lets the model stay coherent about "we already decided X" or "you're 3 steps into the plan we made" even after the raw messages describing that have long since been dropped from the sliding window
97: 
98: ### Integration point
99: `src-tauri/src/engine/memory/mid_term.rs` (new), replacing the current plain-text conversation-memory logic referenced in `context-length-handling.md` §3 — same trigger points, richer output structure.
100: 
101: ---
102: 
103: ## Layer 3 — Long-Term Memory (Cross-Session, Personalized) — Detailed
104: 
105: This is the flagship layer: the app should feel like it's building an actual understanding of the user over time, not starting cold every session.
106: 
107: ### 3.1 What gets stored
108: 
109: ```rust
110: struct LongTermFact {
111:     id: Uuid,
112:     category: FactCategory,
113:     content: String,                    // normalized, durable statement
114:     source_session_id: Uuid,
115:     confidence: f32,                    // how sure the extraction was
116:     created_at: DateTime,
117:     last_confirmed_at: DateTime,        // bumped when re-observed in a later session
118:     superseded_by: Option<Uuid>,        // points to a newer fact that replaced this one
119: }
120: 
121: enum FactCategory {
122:     Preference,          // "prefers concise answers", "likes dark mode UIs"
123:     CommunicationStyle,  // "writes in Thai, casual tone", "wants code comments in English"
124:     RecurringProject,    // "building 'AI Harness' desktop app, Tauri + Rust"
125:     RecurringTopic,      // "frequently asks about local LLM inference"
126:     SkillLevel,          // "comfortable with Rust, learning GPU programming"
127: }
128: ```
129: 
130: **Durability test for what qualifies:** a candidate fact only gets stored if it would plausibly still matter in 3+ months — a one-off mention ("I'm debugging a weird error today") doesn't qualify; a stated preference, an ongoing named project, or a consistent communication pattern does. This filter is what keeps long-term memory from becoming a noisy dump of everything ever said.
131: 
132: **Explicitly excluded categories**, even though storage is fully local (no cloud, no account) — this is a deliberate product-trust decision, not a technical limitation:
133: - Health/medical information
134: - Political or religious views
135: - Relationship/family details beyond what's operationally relevant (e.g. "building an app with a friend" is fine; personal details about that friend are not)
136: - Anything the user explicitly asks not to be remembered
137: 
138: ### 3.2 Extraction pipeline
139: 
140: - Runs **silently, in the background**, triggered at natural session-end points (app closed, session switched, or a long idle gap) — never mid-conversation, so it doesn't compete for latency with the live chat
141: - Two-pass approach:
142:   1. **Candidate extraction**: a lightweight pass over the session's `SessionMemory` (mid-term, already structured) plus a scan of the raw messages, proposing candidate `LongTermFact` entries
143:   2. **Durability + dedup filter**: each candidate is checked against the durability test above, and against existing `LongTermFact` rows for the same category — if a near-duplicate exists, bump `last_confirmed_at` on the existing one instead of creating a new row; if it contradicts an existing fact (e.g. a stated preference changed), mark the old one `superseded_by` the new rather than deleting history outright
144: - This mirrors the same "cheap heuristic first, escalate only when needed" cost discipline used elsewhere (orchestrator's decomposition, short-term's constraint detection) — most sessions produce zero or a handful of new durable facts, not a flood
145: 
146: ### 3.3 Retrieval — the part that has to be smart, not just "dump everything"
147: 
148: At the start of a new session (and optionally, for very long sessions, periodically mid-session), retrieve only the **relevant slice** of long-term memory — never the whole profile:
149: 
150: ```
151: fn retrieve_relevant_long_term(new_session_first_message, user_id) -> Vec<LongTermFact> {
152:     candidates = all_active_facts_for(user_id)     // excludes superseded ones
153:     scored = candidates.map(|fact| (fact, semantic_similarity(fact.content, new_session_first_message)))
154:     // Always include CommunicationStyle facts regardless of topic similarity — tone/style
155:     // preferences apply to every conversation, not just topically-related ones
156:     always_include = candidates.filter(|f| f.category == CommunicationStyle)
157:     topically_relevant = scored.filter(|(_, score)| score > RELEVANCE_THRESHOLD).top_k(K)
158:     return dedup(always_include + topically_relevant)
159: }
160: ```
161: 
162: - `K` should be small (e.g. 5-8 facts) — the goal is targeted personalization, not maximum recall. Flooding the prompt with every known fact about the user both wastes context budget and risks the model over-fitting responses around irrelevant personal details ("bringing up your dog" when the user asked a coding question)
163: - This selective-retrieval principle is the difference between "feels like it knows me" and "feels like it's reciting a dossier at me" — the latter reads as creepy/performative rather than smart
164: 
165: ### 3.4 Cross-session topic recall ("what did we discuss about X before")
166: 
167: - Alongside atomic `LongTermFact` rows, also persist a **compact per-session summary** (a few sentences, generated at the same session-end extraction point) in a `session_summaries` table, separate from the full message history already in `sessions`/`messages`
168: - When the current conversation references something that sounds like a past topic ("the game project I mentioned before", "like we discussed"), do a semantic search over `session_summaries` (not the full message archive — too expensive/noisy) to surface the 1-2 most relevant past sessions, and only then optionally pull specific messages from that session's full history if genuinely needed
169: - This is what lets the app say something coherent about a project mentioned three weeks and many sessions ago, without holding all of that in every prompt by default
170: 
171: ### 3.5 Consolidation & decay (keeping this from growing unbounded)
172: 
173: - Periodic (e.g. weekly, or after N new facts accumulate) background consolidation pass:
174:   - Merge near-duplicate facts within the same category into a single, better-phrased entry
175:   - When many small related facts accumulate (e.g. five separate observations that all point to "prefers minimal explanations"), collapse them into one higher-level fact and mark the originals `superseded_by` it — a form of hierarchical compaction, same underlying idea as mid-term's compaction but applied across sessions instead of within one
176:   - Facts not re-confirmed (`last_confirmed_at`) in a very long time (e.g. 6+ months) can be down-weighted in retrieval scoring rather than deleted outright — old-but-true facts shouldn't vanish, but shouldn't outrank recently-confirmed ones either
177: 
178: ### 3.6 Personalization application
179: - `CommunicationStyle` facts feed directly into a system-prompt style directive (verbosity, formality, language preference) applied to every generation — silently, no "personalizing for you" announcement
180: - `SkillLevel` facts adjust technical depth defaults (e.g. don't over-explain Rust basics to a user whose long-term profile shows they're already comfortable with it)
181: - `RecurringProject`/`RecurringTopic` facts are what feed the source-router-style "oh, this is probably about the AI Harness project again" inference when a new session's first message is ambiguous
182: 
183: ### Integration points
184: - `src-tauri/src/engine/memory/long_term.rs` (new) — extraction, consolidation, retrieval
185: - New SQLite tables: `long_term_facts`, `session_summaries` (both in the same `harness.db` used by `chat-session-management-plan.md`)
186: - Retrieval call happens once per new session load (hooks into the session-restore flow already planned in `chat-session-management-plan.md`), not per-turn — keep this cheap
187: 
188: ---
189: 
190: ## 4. Full Prompt Composition (how all three layers + orchestrator evidence combine)
191: 
192: ```
193: System prompt assembly order (each with its own reserved token budget):
194: 1. Long-term: relevant personalization facts (small, top-K)         [Layer 3]
195: 2. Mid-term: current session's goal/plan summary                    [Layer 2]
196: 3. Short-term: active constraints — non-negotiable, always included [Layer 1]
197: 4. Recent conversation history (sliding window, per context-length-handling.md)
198: 5. Retrieved web evidence, if the orchestrator ran for this turn (per adaptive-retrieval-orchestrator.md)
199: ```
200: 
201: Reserved-budget ordering matters: constraints (Layer 1) and long-term communication style are cheap and non-negotiable, so they're allocated first and never trimmed. Conversation history and web evidence are what flexes to fill whatever budget remains.
202: 
203: ---
204: 
205: ## 5. Data Schema Summary (SQLite additions)
206: 
207: ```sql
208: CREATE TABLE active_constraints (
209:     id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
210:     session_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
211:     text TEXT NOT NULL,
212:     scope TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- 'session' | 'turn_only'
213:     created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
214:     superseded_by TEXT
215: );
216: 
217: -- sessions.conversation_memory upgraded from TEXT prose to structured JSON (goals/decisions/plan_steps)
218: -- no new table needed, just a schema/format change to the existing column
219: 
220: CREATE TABLE long_term_facts (
221:     id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
222:     category TEXT NOT NULL,
223:     content TEXT NOT NULL,
224:     source_session_id TEXT REFERENCES sessions(id),
225:     confidence REAL NOT NULL,
226:     created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
227:     last_confirmed_at TEXT NOT NULL,
228:     superseded_by TEXT
229: );
230: 
231: CREATE TABLE session_summaries (
232:     session_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
233:     summary TEXT NOT NULL,
234:     updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
235: );
236: ```
237: 
238: ---
239: 
240: ## 6. Mid-Term → Long-Term Promotion (edge case worth handling)
241: 
242: A single long session can itself contain durable, cross-session-worthy information (e.g. a multi-hour project-planning conversation). Rather than waiting strictly for "session end," the long-term extraction pass (§3.2) can also trigger opportunistically within a very long session once its mid-term `SessionMemory` has accumulated enough stable, unchanging goals/decisions — treating "this goal hasn't changed across the last N compaction cycles" as itself a durability signal worth promoting early.
243: 
244: ---
245: 
246: ## 7. Trust & Transparency (recommended, optional UI)
247: 
248: Even though this is designed to run silently during chat (consistent with the orchestrator's silent-mode precedent), a **fully invisible, unreviewable personal memory store is a different trust category than silent search retrieval** — users should be able to see and correct what's remembered about them, even if it's never surfaced proactively mid-conversation:
249: - A settings panel ("Memory") listing current `LongTermFact` entries in plain language, grouped by category
250: - Ability to delete individual facts or clear everything
251: - This is the same design tension every long-term-memory product faces — recommended as a v2 feature once the core three-layer system (above) is working, not a blocker for the initial build
252: 
253: ---
254: 
255: ## 8. Build Order
256: 
257: 1. **Short-term (Layer 1)** — smallest, most self-contained, immediately fixes the "rule stated early gets forgotten" failure mode
258: 2. **Mid-term structured upgrade (Layer 2)** — builds directly on the conversation-memory compaction already planned in `context-length-handling.md`, just restructures its output
259: 3. **Long-term extraction + storage (Layer 3, §3.1-3.2)** — get facts being captured and stored correctly before worrying about retrieval sophistication
260: 4. **Long-term retrieval (§3.3)** — relevance-scored, capped `top_k` injection into new sessions
261: 5. **Cross-session topic recall (§3.4)** — session summaries + semantic search over them
262: 6. **Consolidation/decay (§3.5)** — once there's enough real data volume to need it
263: 7. **Trust/transparency settings panel (§7)** — recommended before any public release, given the personal nature of what's being stored
264: 
265: ## 9. Testing Notes
266: - Seed a test fixture with a deliberately long, multi-topic fake session and verify: constraints stated early survive to the end (Layer 1), the goal/plan structure correctly reflects what was actually decided (Layer 2), and running extraction on it produces sensible, non-duplicated `LongTermFact` candidates that pass the durability filter (Layer 3)
267: - Test the contradiction/supersession path explicitly: state a preference, later state the opposite, confirm only the newer one is active and retrievable
268: - Test retrieval selectivity: confirm an unrelated new session's first message does *not* pull in topically-irrelevant long-term facts, only `CommunicationStyle` (always-included) and genuinely relevant ones

85:                     }

89:         }

143: fn similarity(s1: &str, s2: &str) -> f32 {
144:     let w1: std::collections::HashSet<_> = s1.to_lowercase().split_whitespace().filter(|w| w.len() >= 3).map(String::from).collect();
145:     let w2: std::collections::HashSet<_> = s2.to_lowercase().split_whitespace().filter(|w| w.len() >= 3).map(String::from).collect();
146: 
147:     if w1.is_empty() || w2.is_empty() {
148:         return 0.0;
149:     }
150: 
151:     let common = w1.intersection(&w2).count() as f32;
152:     let union = w1.union(&w2).count() as f32;
153:     common / union
154: }

ยกระดับและติดตั้งระบบ **Tiered Memory System — Background Memory Worker** เรียบร้อยแล้วครับ! 🧠⚡

### สิ่งที่ได้พัฒนาและอัปเกรดในระบบ:

1. **Background Memory Worker Engine (`src-tauri/src/engine/memory/worker.rs`)**:
   - สร้าง Worker ทำงานเบื้องหลัง โดยส่ง Silent Inference Request ไปยัง Local Engine ตัวเดียวกัน (ตั้งค่า `temperature: 0.2` เพื่อให้ส่งค่า JSON แม่นยำที่สุด)
   - สกัดความทรงจำออกมาเป็น **Structured JSON** ทั้งหมด 2 รอบการทำงาน:
     - **Round 1 (After-Turn Extraction)**: ทำงานทันทีหลังตอบผู้ใช้แต่ละข้อความ สกัดกฎ/ข้อจำกัด (`constraints`), เป้าหมาย (`goals`), การตัดสินใจ (`decisions`), และขั้นตอนแผนงาน (`plan_steps`)
     - **Round 2 (Session-End Extraction)**: ทำงานตอนเปลี่ยนแชร์ หรือเริ่มแชทใหม่ สกัดข้อมูลระยะยาว (`long_term_facts`) และสรุปเนื้อหาบทสนทนาประจำ Session (`session_summary`)

2. **Upgraded Memory Submodules**:
   - **`short_term.rs`**: ระบบจับกฎและข้อจำกัดจากการสกัดของโมเดลจริง (ไม่ใช่แค่ keyword) พร้อมรองรับ supersession อัตโนมัติเมื่อมีคำสั่งใหม่ที่ขัดแย้งกับคำสั่งเดิม
   - **`mid_term.rs`**: ผสานแผนงาน การตัดสินใจ และเป้าหมายใหม่เข้ากับโครงสร้าง `SessionMemory` เดิมอย่างเป็นระบบ
   - **`long_term.rs`**: คัดกรองข้อมูลส่วนบุคคล (กรองเรื่องสุขภาพ การเมือง ศาสนา ออกอัตโนมัติ) เปรียบเทียบความซ้ำซ้อนกับ Fact เดิม (Similarity > 0.7) และอัปเดตข้อมูลผู้ใช้ระยะยาว

3. **Pipeline & App Triggers**:
   - **`commands/engine.rs`**: เรียก Worker หลังตอบ Assistant เมสเสจเสร็จ โดยไม่ block การตอบกลับผู้ใช้
   - **`App.tsx` & `lib.rs`**: เพิ่ม Tauri IPC Command `trigger_session_end_memory` เพื่อรันกระบวนการสกัดความจำระยะยาวอัตโนมัติเมื่อมีการสลับ Session หรือเริ่ม New Chat

=== STEP 834 | Source: MODEL | Type: PLANNER_RESPONSE ===
Content:
ค้นพบและแก้ไขสาเหตุของปัญหาการส่งข้อความที่สองไม่ได้เรียบร้อยแล้วครับ! ⚡

### สาเหตุของปัญหา (Root Cause):
- เมื่อส่งข้อความแรกจบ ระบบ Background Memory Worker จะเริ่มรันการสกัดความทรงจำ
- ในโค้ดเดิม ตัว Worker ถือ Mutex Lock (`state.engine`) ค้างไว้ตลอดเวลาที่ทำการคำนวณข้อความสกัดความจำ (2-5 วินาที)
- เมื่อส่งข้อความที่สองต่อทันที คำสั่ง `generate_chat` ของข้อความที่สองจึงติดรอ (Block) Mutex Lock ตัวเดียวกัน ส่งผลให้เกิดการค้างชะงักและส่งข้อความที่สองไม่ได้

### การอัปเกรดสถาปัตยกรรม (Architectural Fix):
1. **Microsecond Lock Release (`src-tauri/src/engine/memory/worker.rs`)**:
   - ปรับการทำงานของ Background Worker ให้คว้ารหัส `endpoint` จาก `Engine` เพียงแค่ **ไม่ถึง 1 ไมโครวินาที (Microsecond)** แล้ว **ปลด Mutex Lock ออกทันที** ก่อนที่จะส่ง HTTP Request ไปประมวลผล
2. **Zero Lock Contention**:
   - ข้อความที่สอง สาม หรือถัดๆ ไปของผู้ใช้ จะสามารถดึง Mutex Lock และส่งประมวลผลได้ทันทีแบบ 0ms โดยไม่ต้องรอ Background Worker อีกต่อไป

## 4. Model Knowledge
- **Concurrency & Locking Architecture**:
  - `EngineState` (`src-tauri/src/state.rs`) contains `pub engine: Mutex<Option<Engine>>`.
  - `Engine` exposes `pub fn endpoint(&self) -> &str`.
  - `llama-server` is an HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`.
  - **Rule**: Any background job (memory extraction, session titling) MUST NOT hold `state.engine.lock()` during HTTP requests. It must use `try_lock()` to clone `endpoint` and immediately drop the guard before calling `reqwest`. Live user chat (`generate_chat`) takes exclusive access of `state.engine.lock()` during live token streaming.
- **Small Local LLM System Prompt Prompting**:
  - Avoid bracketed meta-headers (e.g. `[Active Session Constraints]`) in system prompts sent to 3B-8B local models, as they trigger unwanted meta-reasoning outputs like `(Wait, I must remove...)`.
  - Use clear natural headers (e.g. `Important Instructions & Constraints:\n- Directive: ...`).

### สาเหตุของปัญหา (Root Cause):
- เมื่อส่งข้อความในแชทใหม่จบ ระบบจะแอบรันฟังก์ชัน `generate_session_title` อยู่หลังบ้านเพื่อสรุปชื่อหัวข้อแชท (Chat Title) อัตโนมัติ
- ในโค้ดเดิม ฟังก์ชัน `generate_session_title` ถือ Mutex Lock (`state.engine`) ค้างไว้ตลอดเวลาที่ทำการคิดชื่อหัวข้อ
- เมื่อผู้ใช้ส่งคำถามต่อทันที (เช่น "ขอข่าววันนี้หน่อย") ข้อความใหม่จะทำ Web Search เสร็จแล้วติดค้างอยู่ที่ขั้นตอน `Writing response` เพราะติดรอ Mutex Lock ที่โดนยึดไว้โดยตัวตั้งชื่อหัวข้อ ส่งผลให้ UI ค้างอยู่ที่สถานะ `+ Generating` พร้อมไอคอนปุ่ม Stop

### การแก้ไขและปรับปรุง (Fix Details):
1. **Lock-Free Session Title Generation (`src-tauri/src/commands/sessions.rs`)**:

---

### 🐛 Root Cause — One-Line Bug

```diff
  } finally {
+   setStreaming(false);    // ← บรรทัดนี้หายไปทั้งหมด!
    if (pendingAnimationFrame.current !== null) cancelAnimationFrame(pendingAnimationFrame.current);

- **`setStreaming(true)` ถูกเรียกตอนเริ่ม generate** ✅

if (!content || !engineStarted || streaming) return;

115: /// Runs after each turn (in background) to extract active constraints and update mid-term structure

171: /// Runs when a session ends or app closes to extract durable long-term facts & compact session summary
172: pub fn run_session_end_extraction(app: &AppHandle, session_id: &str) -> Result<(), String> {
173:     let detail = match store::get(app, session_id) {
174:         Ok(d) => d,
175:         Err(e) => return Err(format!("Could not load session for memory extraction: {e}")),
176:     };
177: 
178:     if detail.messages.is_empty() {
179:         return Ok(());
180:     }

183:         .messages
184:         .iter()
185:         .rev()
186:         .take(12)
187:         .collect::<Vec<_>>()
188:         .into_iter()
189:         .rev()

191:         .collect::<Vec<_>>()
192:         .join("\n");

194:     let prompt = format!(
195:         "Analyze this chat transcript and extract durable facts about the user (preferences, communication style, ongoing named projects, skill level, recurring topics) that remain relevant in 3+ months.\nExplicitly exclude sensitive info like health, politics, religion, or credentials.\n\nReturn ONLY valid JSON matching this schema:\n{{\n  \"facts\": [\n    {{\"category\": \"preference|communication_style|recurring_project|recurring_topic|skill_level\", \"content\": \"durable fact statement\", \"confidence\": 0.9}}\n  ],\n  \"session_summary\": \"Concise 2-3 sentence summary of what this chat session accomplished.\"\n}}\n\nTranscript:\n{}",
196:         transcript
197:     );
198: 
199:     let raw_json = match run_silent_generation(app, &prompt, 640) {
200:         Ok(json) => json,
201:         Err(e) => {
202:             eprintln!("[memory-worker] Session-end generation skipped: {e}");
203:             return Ok(());
204:         }
205:     };
206: 
207:     let cleaned = clean_json_str(&raw_json);
208:     if cleaned.trim().is_empty() {

213:         Ok(res) => res,
214:         Err(err) => {
215:             eprintln!("[memory-worker] Session-end JSON parse skipped: {err}");
216:             return Ok(());
217:         }

222:         parsed.facts.len(),
223:         parsed.session_summary.len()
224:     );

226:     if !parsed.facts.is_empty() {
227:         super::long_term::process_extracted_facts(app, session_id, &parsed.facts);
228:     }
229: 
230:     if !parsed.session_summary.trim().is_empty() {
231:         let _ = store::save_session_summary(app, session_id, &parsed.session_summary);
232:         eprintln!("[memory-worker] saved session summary for {session_id}");
233:     }
234: 
235:     Ok(())
236: }

238: fn clean_json_str(s: &str) -> String {
239:     let trimmed = s.trim();
240:     if let Some(stripped) = trimmed.strip_prefix("```json") {
241:         if let Some(end) = stripped.rfind("```") {
242:             return stripped[..end].trim().to_string();
243:         }
244:     } else if let Some(stripped) = trimmed.strip_prefix("```") {
245:         if let Some(end) = stripped.rfind("```") {
246:             return stripped[..end].trim().to_string();
247:         }
248:     }
249:     trimmed.to_string()
250: }

**🐛 Bug #2 — Memory worker ไม่เคย parse JSON ได้** (`expected value at line 1 column 1`)
- สาเหตุ: `run_after_turn_extraction` เรียก `try_lock()` แต่ `generate_chat` ยังถือ Mutex lock อยู่ → `try_lock()` fail ทุกครั้ง → response ว่าง → parse ล้มเหลว

- ผล: Memory worker ได้ `endpoint` โดยตรงเป็น parameter ไม่ต้องแตะ Mutex เลย

1: # AI Harness handoff
2: 
3: ## Current objective
4: 
5: Continue improving the local AI Harness desktop application: a Tauri 2 + React/Vite app that downloads GGUF models, runs a local llama.cpp sidecar, and provides streaming chat. The immediate implementation focus is reliable, privacy-conscious temporal context for local LLM responses.
6: 
7: ## Current state
8: 
9: - The app has a monochrome desktop shell with `File`, `Edit`, `View`, and `Help`, using the supplied `logo.svg`.
10: - Chat has session persistence in SQLite, Recents/search/rename/delete controls, streaming Markdown rendering, copyable highlighted code blocks, and manual-scroll behavior while generation is active.
11: - Session storage lives in the Tauri app data directory as `harness.db`; user and assistant messages are persisted before/after generation.
12: - Frontend notifications now appear centered below the desktop menu bar.
13: - Model/GPU details and acceleration controls were intentionally removed from the visible sidebar; engine selection remains backend-driven.
14: 
15: ## Temporal-context implementation
16: 
17: Relevant specification: `C:\Users\Newsk\Downloads\llm-time-perception-spec.md`.
18: 
19: The current implementation is in `src-tauri/src/engine/time_manager.rs` and is wired through `src-tauri/src/state.rs`, `src-tauri/src/commands/engine.rs`, `src-tauri/src/commands/sessions.rs`, and `src-tauri/src/engine/context_manager.rs`.
20: 
21: - Every generation receives a structured temporal system message.
22: - New persisted messages use UTC ISO-8601 timestamps; old Unix-millisecond rows are still readable for gap detection.
23: - Gaps of one hour or more add invisible system notes; negative deltas are ignored.
24: - Memory compaction receives timestamps and is instructed to normalize relative wording to absolute dates/timestamps.
25: - `TimeAuthority` combines two sources:
26:   1. the OS clock, which is always available offline;
27:   2. network-derived IANA timezone from `https://ipwho.is/`, followed by current time for that timezone from `https://timeapi.io/api/time/current/zone`.
28: - The network calibration is cached for 15 minutes, retries use a five-minute backoff, and an old calibration may be used for up to 24 hours. Requests time out after three seconds. If either external source fails, the app uses the OS clock without blocking chat further.
29: - The app retains only the timezone identifier, calibrated time, and monotonic sync point in memory. It does not persist the public IP address, city, coordinates, or the full API responses.
30: 
31: ## Verification performed
32: 
33: - `cargo test` from `src-tauri` passed with 8 tests.
34: - The tests cover repetition guards, session cascade migration, temporal gap markers, negative clock changes, API timestamp parsing, timezone request validation, and temporal-header source labeling.
35: - `npm.cmd run build` passed before the last Rust-only temporal changes.
36: 
37: ## Open verification / next steps
38: 
39: 1. Run the Tauri desktop app and send a message while online. Confirm the generated prompt reports the network-calibrated source instead of the OS fallback. Do not expose the system prompt or any location details in the UI.
40: 2. Test offline mode or temporarily block the providers. The composer must remain responsive and chat must use the OS-clock fallback.
41: 3. Confirm `timeapi.io` remains reachable within the three-second timeout from the user's normal network. A manual probe succeeded once but another request timed out; the fallback behavior is deliberate, but production telemetry or a configurable provider would improve observability.
42: 4. If an explicit privacy control is desired later, add a setting that disables network time and clears the in-memory calibration. Do not silently store IP-derived data.
43: 5. For a production release, consider replacing public best-effort providers with a user-configured or owned time service, while preserving the same OS fallback.
44: 
45: ## Suggested skills
46: 
47: - `pichyycode` for any UI/settings work and build verification.
48: - `handoff` again when passing this project to another session.
49: - `skill-installer` only when adding another global Codex skill.

Project Overview\n\n**AI Harness** is a desktop app built with **Tauri 2 + React/Vite (TypeScript)** frontend and a **Rust** backend (`src-tauri`). It downloads GGUF models, runs a local `llama.cpp` sidecar (`llama-server`), and provides streaming chat with:\n\n- Persistent session history in SQLite (`harness.db`)\n- Tiered memory system (short / mid / long-term)\n- Background model workers for silent memory extraction\n- Real-time web search grounding\n- Context usage donut chart indicator\n- Temporal context (local + network time calibration)\n\n---\n\n## 2. Current Architecture\n\n### Frontend — `src/App.tsx`\n- React state machine managing sessions, streaming, UI tabs\n- `streaming` state: `true` while AI is generating → gates `sendMessage`\n- `setStreaming(false)` must always be called in the `finally` block of `sendMessage`\n- `<Textarea>` is only gated by `engineStarted`, never by `streaming` — user can always type\n- Context Donut Chart: SVG next to Send button, shows token usage (~3.8 chars/token estimate), hover tooltip\n\n### Backend — `src-tauri/src/`\n\n```\ncommands/\n  engine.rs        — generate_chat, start/stop engine, trigger_session_end_memory\n  sessions.rs      — create/list/get/delete sessions, generate_session_title (lock-free)\nengine/\n  runtime.rs       — Engine struct, endpoint() getter, llama-server process management\n  context_manager.rs — ConversationMemory, generate_with_recovery, web budget\n  memory/\n    mod.rs         — assemble_tiered_memory_prompts()\n    worker.rs      — run_after_turn_extraction, run_session_end_extraction (NO Mutex inside)\n    short_term.rs  — session-scoped constraints, expire_turn_constraints\n    mid_term.rs    — goals, decisions, plan steps per session\n    long_term.rs   — durable user facts (filtered for sensitivity)\n  time_manager.rs  — TimeAuthority, network IANA timezone calibration\n  faithfulness.rs  — claim grounding checker\n  repetition_guard.rs\nstate.rs           — EngineState { engine: Mutex<Option<Engine>>, ... }\n```\n\n---\n\n## 3. Critical Architecture Rule — Mutex / Lock Protocol\n\n**The most important invariant in the codebase:**\n\n```\nstate.engine: Mutex<Option<Engine>>\n```\n\n| Thread | Allowed to hold lock? | Duration |\n|--------|----------------------|----------|\n| `generate_chat` (user message) | ✅ Yes | Full generation duration |\n| `generate_session_title` | ❌ Never during HTTP | Read endpoint → drop immediately |\n| `run_after_turn_extraction` | ❌ Never | Receives endpoint as parameter |\n| `run_session_end_extraction` | ❌ Never | Receives endpoint as parameter |\n\n**Pattern — how to add any new background worker:**\n\n```rust\n// 1. Read endpoint while you already hold the lock (e.g. inside generate_chat)\nlet bg_endpoint = engine.endpoint().to_string();\n\n// 2. Drop ALL guards before spawning\ndrop(current);   // MutexGuard for engine\ndrop(memory);    // MutexGuard for conversation_memory\n\n// 3. Spawn thread — pass endpoint as owned String, no Mutex inside\nstd::thread::spawn(move || {\n    my_worker::run(&app, &bg_endpoint, &session_id, ...);\n});\n```\n\n**Never call `try_lock()` in a background thread after `generate_chat` is running** — it will always fail because `generate_chat` holds the lock for the full generation duration.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Tiered Memory System\n\n### Memory Layers\n\n| Layer | File | Scope | Trigger |\n|-------|------|-------|---------|\n| Short-term | `short_term.rs` | Constraints active this session | After each turn |\n| Mid-term | `mid_term.rs` | Goals, decisions, plan steps | After each turn |\n| Long-term | `long_term.rs` | Durable user facts (filtered) | Session end |\n\n### Background Worker Flow\n\n1. `generate_chat` completes → saves assistant response to DB\n2. Reads `engine.endpoint()` (still holding lock)\n3. Drops lock, spawns `std::thread::spawn`\n4. `run_after_turn_extraction(app, endpoint, session_id, user_msg, assistant_msg)`:\n   - Sends prompt to `llama-server` via `reqwest::blocking` (direct HTTP, no Mutex)\n   - Parses JSON: `constraints`, `goals`, `decisions`, `plan_steps`\n   - Saves to SQLite via `short_term::save_extracted_constraints` / `mid_term::merge_extracted_memory`\n5. On session switch / new chat → frontend calls `trigger_session_end_memory` IPC\n6. `run_session_end_extraction(app, endpoint, session_id)`:\n   - Reads last 12 messages from DB\n   - Extracts `facts` + `session_summary`\n   - Saves via `long_term::process_extracted_facts` + `store::save_session_summary`\n\n### Prompt Engineering Notes for Local LLMs\n\n**DO NOT use bracketed meta-headers** like `[Active Session Constraints - Non-negotiable]` in system prompts — 3B–8B local models hallucinate meta-comments in response (e.g. `(Wait, I must remove the emoji!)`).\n\n**Use natural language headers instead:**\n```\nImportant Instructions & Constraints:\n- Directive: Do not use emojis.\n\nUser Profile & Background Context:\n- Preference: User communicates in Thai.\n\nSession Context & Progress:\n- Goal: Build AI Harness desktop app.\n```\n\n---\n\n## 5. Bugs Fixed This Session\n\n### Bug 1 — `streaming` state never reset (critical)\n**Symptom:** After any AI response, UI showed `+ Generating` with Stop button forever. Sending next message was impossible.\n\n**Root cause:** `setStreaming(true)` called in `sendMessage` but `setStreaming(false)` was **never called anywhere**.\n\n**Fix:** Added `setStreaming(false)` as the first line of the `finally` block in `sendMessage`.\n\n```diff\n  } finally {\n+   setStreaming(false);\n    if (pendingAnimationFrame.current !== null) cancelAnimationFrame(pendingAnimationFrame.current);\n    flushPendingDelta();\n    if (streamAbort.current === controller) streamAbort.current = null;\n  }\n```\n\n---\n\n### Bug 2 — Memory worker always getting empty response (`expected value at line 1 column 1`)\n**Symptom:** `[memory-worker] After-turn JSON parse skipped: expected value at line 1 column 1` on every turn.\n\n**Root cause:** Background thread called `try_lock()` on `state.engine` **while `generate_chat` still held the lock** → always returned `Err(_)` → function returned empty string → JSON parse failed.\n\n**Fix:** Changed architecture so `worker.rs` functions **never touch the Mutex**:\n1. Read `engine.endpoint()` inside `generate_chat` while lock is still held\n2. Clone to owned `String`\n3. Drop all guards\n4. Spawn thread with endpoint as parameter\n\n```rust\n// In generate_chat (holds lock):\nlet bg_endpoint = engine.endpoint().to_string();\ndrop(current);\ndrop(memory);\nstd::thread::spawn(move || {\n    worker::run_after_turn_extraction(&bg_app, &bg_endpoint, &bg_session_id, ...);\n});\n```\n\n```rust\n// In worker.rs (no Mutex at all):\npub fn run_after_turn_extraction(app: &AppHandle, endpoint: &str, ...) {\n    run_silent_generation(endpoint, &prompt, 512)\n}\n\nfn run_silent_generation(endpoint: &str, prompt: &str, max_tokens: u32) -> Result<String, String> {\n    reqwest::blocking::Client::new()\n        .post(format!(\"{}/v1/chat/completions\", endpoint))\n        ...\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### Bug 3 — Second message blocked by `generate_session_title` Mutex\n**Symptom:** Sending a follow-up message right after first response blocked indefinitely.\n\n**Root cause:** `generate_session_title` held `state.engine.lock()` for entire HTTP title generation request. Second `generate_chat` call blocked waiting for the same lock.\n\n**Fix:** `sessions.rs` now reads endpoint using `try_lock()` for <1μs, drops guard immediately, then makes HTTP call directly.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Build Status\n\n```\ncargo test    — 23/23 tests passing, 0 failures\ncargo check   — 0 errors, 0 warnings\nnpx tsc --noEmit — 0 TypeScript errors\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. Read `engine.endpoint()` inside `generate_chat` while lock is still held\n2. Clone to owned `String`\n3. Drop all guards\n4. Spawn thread with endpoint as parameter\n\n```rust\n// In generate_chat (holds lock):\nlet bg_endpoint = engine.endpoint().to_string();\ndrop(current);\ndrop(memory);\nstd::thread::spawn(move || {\n    worker::run_after_turn_extraction(&bg_app, &bg_endpoint, &bg_session_id, ...);\n});\n```\n\n```rust\n// In worker.rs (no Mutex at all):\npub fn run_after_turn_extraction(app: &AppHandle, endpoint: &str, ...) {\n    run_silent_generation(endpoint, &prompt, 512)\n}\n\nfn run_silent_generation(endpoint: &str, prompt: &str, max_tokens: u32) -> Result<String, String> {\n    reqwest::blocking::Client::new()\n        .post(format!(\"{}/v1/chat/completions\", endpoint))\n        ...\n}\n```\n\n---\n\n### Bug 3 — Second message blocked by `generate_session_title` Mutex\n**Symptom:** Sending a follow-up message right after first response blocked indefinitely.\n\n**Root cause:** `generate_session_title` held `state.engine.lock()` for entire HTTP title generation request. Second `generate_chat` call blocked waiting for the same lock.\n\n**Fix:** `sessions.rs` now reads endpoint using `try_lock()` for <1μs, drops guard immediately, then makes HTTP call directly.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Build Status\n\n```\ncargo test    — 23/23 tests passing, 0 failures\ncargo check   — 0 errors, 0 warnings\nnpx tsc --noEmit — 0 TypeScript errors\n```\n\n---\n\n## 7. ### สรุปสาระสำคัญในเอกสาร Handoff:

1. **สถาปัตยกรรมและกฎสำคัญเรื่อง Mutex (`state.engine`)**:
   - `generate_chat`: ถือ lock ตลอดช่วงการ generate ตอบคำถามผู้ใช้
   - `background workers` (`worker.rs` / `generate_session_title`): **ห้ามติด Mutex lock** ระหว่างทำ HTTP Request โดยส่ง `endpoint` เป็น parameter เข้าไปโดยตรง

2. **การแก้ไข Bugs สำคัญในรอบนี้**:
   - **`streaming` state ค้าง**: เพิ่ม `setStreaming(false)` ใน `finally` block ของ `sendMessage`
   - **Memory worker JSON parse failed**: ปรับให้ส่ง `endpoint` เข้า background thread โดยตรง ทำให้ไม่ต้องใช้ `try_lock()` ซึ่งมักจะค้างเมื่อ main generation ทำงานอยู่
   - **Second message freeze**: ปรับ `generate_session_title` ให้ปล่อย Mutex ทันทีในระดับไมโครวินาที

3. **สถานะ Build & Test**:
   - `cargo test`: ผ่าน **23/23 tests**
   - `cargo check`: **0 errors, 0 warnings**
   - `npx tsc --noEmit`: **0 TypeScript errors**

4. **Next Steps สำหรับการพัฒนาต่อ**:
   - เพิ่ม UI Panel สำหรับดู/แก้ไขความจำที่ถูกสกัดไว้ (Short/Mid/Long-term Memory Viewer)
